Subject: Post-demo: Lumina capacity & SKU calibration / next steps

Thanks again for taking the time today — good discussion. Quick recap and a few asks so we can size the Dedicated path properly (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private).

Highlights from the call:
- Primary workload: anonymized clinical summarization + search reranking for clinician-facing UI. Expected 95th-pct latency target ~400ms for short summaries.
- Traffic shape: bursty daytime traffic (08:00-18:00 local), peak TPS estimate you mentioned ~55 TPM (concurrent requests per minute) which maps to ~0.9 TPS sustained during peaks; please see attached token profile for sample prompts.
- Token mix: short prompts (average 60 tokens input, 120 tokens output) for summaries; occasional long context retrievals up to 2k tokens for research flows.
- Security: must be VPC-only for PHI-sensitive endpoints — interest in Private (VPC) later, but initial ask is Dedicated reserved pool under Redwood with customer-managed VPC peering.

Concrete asks (action items):
1) Dana/Alex: confirm the weekday peak TPS and weekly baseline TPS (please add ranges if you prefer conservative/expected). We used 55 peak TPM today — can you confirm peak TPS or provide logs?
2) Dana: can you share a small sample of prompt mixes separate from PHI (redacted) — we attached lumina_token_profile.csv as a template.
3) Karthik/Ben: can you produce two capacity sketches: (A) Dedicated pool optimized for latency (NVIDIA H100-like class), targeting 50-75 peak TPS with 90% short-token workload; (B) cost-optimized mix using a GPU blend (A100-class + smaller quantized instances) with fallback for long-context jobs?
4) Procurement: Dana, please loop in procurement (procurement@luminahealth.com) if we proceed to an OKR/contract stage — we may need an NDA + SOC2 attestation.

Attachments: lumina_token_profile.csv (redacted sample), redwood_capacity_options.pdf (initial SKU sketches)

Proposed next touch: internal sizing deliverable from Karthik by EOD Jul 30, then a 30-min follow-up working session week of Aug 3 to align on VM/GPU mix and network setup.

Best,
Irene

Thanks Irene — this is helpful. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

- Peak numbers: apologies for the shorthand on the call. 55 TPM was a minutes-based number — our actual observed peak concurrent requests during last week’s pilot were about 1.2 TPS sustained for ~12 minutes during the morning surge. For planning, we should use peak TPS = 1.5 to give headroom.
- Baseline: typical daytime baseline is ~0.25 TPS. Nighttime near zero.
- Token split: ~88% short summaries (avg 180 total tokens combined), ~10% mid-length (<=512 tokens), ~2% long (>512 tokens).
- VPC requirement: we are evaluating both Dedicated (with private peering) and Private deployment (customer-managed control plane). For the POC we prefer Dedicated to avoid onboarding ops overhead, then move to Private if we validate PHI handling and throughput.

I attached a redacted sample of a busy-day log snippet (redacted for PHI) — that should help with exact concurrency and tail latencies. We can also run a short synthetic spike test if you prefer.

Happy to retime the follow-up to early next week.

Dana Brooks
Head of AI Platforms | Lumina Health
dana.brooks@luminahealth.com | +1 650-555-0177

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Dana Brooks <dana.brooks@luminahealth.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Lumina capacity & SKU calibration / next steps

Thanks Dana — that clarification is great and materially changes the sizing. Quick internal note on options (high-level):

Option A (latency-first):
- Target: 1.5 TPS sustained peak, 400ms P95 for short summaries.
- SKU: 2 x H100-class instances in a dedicated pool with autoscale headroom + 1 smaller instance for long-context batching.
- Concurrency strategy: per-request routing to low-latency pool for short summaries, long-context routed to quantified instances with KV-cache warmers.
- Pros: meets latency SLO, simple routing.
- Cons: higher unit cost.

Option B (cost-balanced):
- Target: same peak TPS but accept P95 up to ~600ms for non-critical flows.
- SKU: Mixed pool: A100-class for most short summaries (quantized), plus spot-like burst capacity using lower-cost accelerators for background/long-context jobs.
- Concurrency: more aggressive batching for mid/long jobs, prefix caching for repeated prompts.
- Pros: 20-30% cost reduction in projected token-unit cost.
- Cons: slightly higher latency tail.

Next steps I will deliver this afternoon: rough cost curves, expected P95 estimates by SKU, and a recommended initial config to show in the follow-up session. If Lumina can run the synthetic spike (Dana), we can validate the autoscale thresholds.

-Karthik
